name: Percent Live Births by Infant Sex and Mother’s Race/Ethnicity
description:
This dataset contains annual figures on live births in the United States, broken down by infant sex and the mother's race or ethnicity, covering birth years 2007 through 2023. Each row represents a combination of birth year, infant sex (male or female), and one of seven maternal race/ethnicity categories, including Non-Hispanic White, Non-Hispanic Black, Hispanic, Asian/Pacific Islander, and Other. For each combination, the dataset reports the number of births and the corresponding percentage, allowing users to see both raw counts and relative shares.

The data can be used to examine trends over time, such as changes in the sex ratio at birth or shifts in the demographic composition of births. It supports comparisons across racial and ethnic groups, year-over-year analysis, and descriptive statistics or visualizations for public health reporting. Researchers, analysts, and policymakers could use it for equity-focused reporting, trend analysis, and exploratory studies of birth outcomes by demographic group.
